title: List and inspect
summary: List ordinary and hidden names, read long-list metadata, distinguish files from directories, and print a short text file.

content.objective: Use ls, ls -a, ls -l, and cat to inspect a directory without changing it, including hidden names, file-versus-directory metadata, and short text contents.
content.instructions: Inspect the supplied workspace in order. First list ordinary names, then reveal hidden names, read the long metadata listing for field-notes, and finally print observations.txt. Do not create, rename, or remove anything.

tasks.title: List the ordinary names
tasks.instructions: Run plain ls in the current workspace. Its output should include README.txt and field-notes. Notice that the dot-prefixed manifest is not shown by this ordinary listing.

tasks.title: Reveal the hidden manifest
tasks.instructions: List all names in the current workspace, including dot-prefixed names. Find .manifest.txt in the output.

tasks.title: Distinguish files from a directory
tasks.instructions: Request a long listing of field-notes. Use the first character of each entry line to confirm that archive is a directory while observations.txt and supplies.txt are regular files. Exact owners, sizes, and times are not important.

tasks.title: Read the observations
tasks.instructions: Use cat with the relative path field-notes/observations.txt. Read the three lines printed to the terminal and leave the fixture unchanged.

hints.text: Use the listing command from the lesson with no option and no path.
The command is two letters long. Check the final names in its output.
Ordinary listings omit names whose first character is a dot. Add the option meaning all.
The all option is -a; keep the command focused on the current directory.
Ask ls for its long format and give field-notes as the path to inspect.
Use -l. In the output, d begins a directory line and - begins a regular-file line.
Use the read-only command that prints a short text file, followed by the file's relative path.
The command is cat, and the path starts with field-notes/.

tutor.goalSummary: Student independently selects ls, ls -a, ls -l, and cat to inspect fixed workspace names, metadata, and short text while explaining hidden-name and entry-type cues.
misconceptions: ls lists a directory but does not enter it or change the current working directory.
A leading dot makes a name hidden from ordinary ls output; it does not encrypt or protect the entry.
In ls -l output, the first character is an entry-type marker: d is a directory and - is a regular file.
Long-list sizes and timestamps are metadata, not file contents, and a directory size is not a recursive total.
cat prints bytes from a file; it is appropriate here only because the target is known short text.
constraints: Keep coaching within ls, ls -a, ls -l, hidden names, basic long-list metadata, and cat.
Do not suggest commands that create, edit, rename, copy, move, or delete workspace entries.
Give hints in level order and ask the student to predict output before revealing an exact command at level 3.
Do not provide all four command lines as a pasteable sequence or complete later tasks for the student.
Judge variable owner names, spacing, sizes, and timestamps as incidental; focus on the leading type character and final entry name.
After success, ask the student to explain why .manifest.txt was hidden and how archive was identified as a directory.
